bottlenecks.reading: Scale-up interconnect inside the AI rack is still copper. SemiAnalysis: Blackwell NVL72 uses approximately five thousand copper cables on the NVLink backplane; Rubin (NVLink 6) doubles bandwidth with bi-directional signalling over the same number of copper cables, and its scale-up network stays on copper, with optics expected only later for larger world sizes. The cable count per rack therefore does not rise from Blackwell to Rubin, so rack content growth has to come from bandwidth-driven price / spec content and other parts. Amphenol is named as exclusive supplier of the DensiLink OverPass cable set in GB200/GB300 compute trays and its PaladinHD2 board-to-board connectors are named for VR NVL72 compute trays; SemiAnalysis reads cableless compute trays as a positive for Amphenol because the signals still need board-to-board connectors. The NVLink spine supplier split (Amphenol, Luxshare, Molex, TE, Volex) was not visible in the part read.

Demand is running ahead of APH's output today, and APH is the one adding the capacity: Q2 2026 orders were a record $10,732M (book-to-bill 1.23, every end market above 1, organic orders +63%); IT datacom was 43% of Q2 sales (about $3.77B), +89% in dollars and +63% organically, with virtually all of its 22% sequential growth from AI-related products; management expects IT datacom up in the mid-teens sequentially in Q3. Capex ran at the high end of 3-4% of sales and is guided modestly higher in the second half. How long the shortage lasts is not stated by the issuer; the Q3 2026 sales guide is $9.3-9.4B (+50% to +52%). Update after the Q3 2026 release (2026-10-28, citable from 2026-10-30): sales $10,229.7M (+65%, +37% organic), orders $12.2B, book-to-bill 1.19:1, Q4 guide $10.3-10.5B (~+60%); the 10-Q says growth was driven by outsized organic IT datacom growth, with AI-related strength in Communications Solutions (+51% organic) and Interconnect and Sensor Systems; communications networks declined organically. Demand still exceeds sales but book-to-bill eased from 1.23 to 1.19.

Connector pricing has turned up in the channel: an Edgewater Research channel summary says Nvidia accepted some higher connector / backplane pricing on next-generation AI racks, connector pricing in the channel is trending higher with further increases expected in June / July, TE is seen benefiting from pricing and content expansion on hyperscale AI programs, and passive component lead times are stretching (capacitors up to 52 weeks, tantalum effectively on allocation). Channel opinion, not audited; it is a margin tailwind to test, not a driver. APH's own Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin included $80M of net tariff recoveries.

How long copper stays the scale-up medium: unnamed channel comments in the Edgewater summary see no optics replacing copper for intra-rack scale-up before 2029 at the earliest and active copper adoption accelerating first; the AI customer mindset is quoted as 'copper when possible, optics when necessary'. Supply-chain sources in the same note flag an elevated risk that Nvidia's Kyber rack slips to 2H28 on midplane / connector challenges. Reach is the structural limit (copper effective reach below about 10 m at high speed, per a secondary site summarising Nomura).

Hypothesis: Nvidia's Kyber generation, with a PCB midplane instead of cable cartridges, removes the cable-cartridge content that Amphenol supplies in Oberon racks, so APH's share of rack content would fall unless its midplane / board-to-board connector and power content offset it. Analyst commentary to that effect appeared in search results but the underlying reports were not read, and the Kyber timing is uncertain (possible slip to 2028).

Fiber is the second scarce thing, and capacity is being added by named rivals: Corning's Optical Communications sales grew 32% to $2,072M in Q2 2026 (Enterprise Networks +65%, AI data-center sales nearly doubled), and Corning with Nvidia plans to expand U.S. optical connectivity manufacturing capacity 10x and U.S. fiber capacity by more than 50%. APH bought CommScope's connectivity and cable business on 2026-01-09: it contributed $2,100.9M of sales through 2026-06-30, is expected to add $4.6B of sales and $0.30 of accretion in 2026 (raised from $4.1B and $0.15), IT datacom is expected to be a bit under half of CommScope's 2026 sales (about a third in 2025), and CommScope's IT datacom business 'essentially doubled' year on year. Update: CommScope's contribution through 2026-09-30 was $3,683.3M of sales (10-Q) and APH raised its 2026 CommScope outlook again to $5.1B sales and $0.18 accretion (release 2026-10-28). Corning's Optical Communications grew 44% to $2,379M in Q3 2026 (Enterprise Networks +84%, Gen AI sales more than doubled; Corning release 2026-10-27), and Corning signed four multibillion-dollar long-term agreements (Verizon, AT&T among them).

Hypothesis: APH (through CommScope) gains hyperscale fiber share because customers want a second source next to Corning after the Nvidia / Corning announcement; this rests on one unnamed channel comment ('Amphenol/CCS is likely among the beneficiaries') in the Edgewater summary and no APH number yet supports it.

Active electrical cables (AEC) are a fast-growing slice of AI copper that APH can now address: Credo's revenue grew 114.7% to $479.0M in its fiscal Q1 2027 and 205.7% to $1,335.1M in fiscal 2026, and Credo settled its patent dispute with Amphenol under a license on 2025-08-14 (Molex and TE moved to terminate their ITC cases on settlement on 2026-03-26). Edgewater's channel checks: Amazon issued a roughly 2M Trn3-related AEC RFQ, Nvidia is exploring AEC for a front-end networking reference design, xAI AEC demand looks paused after February orders pending VR72 deployments, and 1.6T AEC interest is broadening with Meta and xAI projected as major customers. APH's own AEC revenue is not disclosed.

A second named rival confirms the AI interconnect shortage on its own numbers: TE Connectivity's fiscal Q4 2026 orders were $6.1B (+29%), full-year orders $22.2B (+27%) and Industrial Solutions grew 26% in fiscal 2026; TE guides fiscal Q1 2027 sales of about $5.35B (+15%) and FY27 organic growth similar to FY26. APH's Q3 2026 book-to-bill was 1.19 and Q4 guide ~+60% in dollars. Demand for scarce data and power connectivity is broad across the named rivals, not APH-specific.

fd SHARE APH vs TEL: APH IT datacom in Q2 2026 is about $3.77B (43% of $8,758.1M net sales; the 43% is from the call transcript summary, derived dollars), +89% in dollars and +63% organically. TE's data-center-facing Digital Data Networks line was $207M in fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter to 2026-06-26), +34.2% (nine months +48.8%); TE Industrial Solutions grew 21% organically and TE total 12.2%. On these numbers APH's IT datacom is about 18 times TE's DDN and grew about 1.8 times as fast organically. Hypothesis (labelled): APH is gaining share against TE in AI data-center interconnect. Limits: TE also books AI power / energy outside DDN, APH's IT datacom includes servers, storage, networking and acquired fiber, and the dollar growth includes CommScope while the +63% is organic.

fd SHARE APH vs CRDO: Credo grew 114.7% year on year to $479.0M (fiscal Q1 2027) against APH IT datacom +63% organic, so Credo is growing faster from a base about one eighth of APH's IT datacom. AEC adds to rather than replaces passive copper in the same racks, and APH has held an AEC license since 2025-08-14, so this is hypothesis only: Credo gains share of the active in-rack / top-of-rack cable slice while APH's AEC revenue is unknown. Credo's own AEC share claim (~88%, JPMorgan via syndicated posts) is unverified and not used.

fd SHARE APH vs GLW (fiber): Corning Optical Communications +32% to $2,072M, Enterprise Networks +65%, AI data-center sales nearly doubled; APH says CommScope's IT datacom business essentially doubled year on year. Both roughly doubling points to APH holding, not clearly gaining, fiber share (hypothesis; Corning's AI data-center dollars and CommScope's IT datacom dollars are not disclosed).

fd SHARE APH overall: Communications Solutions net sales $5,383.6M in Q2 2026 vs $2,909.8M (+85% in dollars, +42% organic), operating margin 33.6% vs 30.6%, 62% of net sales (pf_rel_20260729_1, pf_10q_20260731); APH consolidated organic growth was +30% in Q2 2026 against TE +12.2% total and Corning core +17%. TE's gross margin is about 35.6% and Corning's 36.1% against Credo about 65-68% (a chip-plus-cable model); APH's own gross margin is gather_numbers' to state.

fd SHARE VERDICT: no attributed share study (Dell'Oro, 650 Group, LightCounting, SemiAnalysis BoM) could be read, so every share reading above is a numbers-based hypothesis, not a measured share. The direction on the numbers is APH ahead of TE, behind Credo in growth rate only on a small base, level with Corning in fiber; Molex, Luxshare, Volex and FIT cannot be quantified. A SemiAnalysis VR NVL72 bill-of-materials model (paid) would name the NVLink spine supplier split.

fd BROADCOM ROLE: Broadcom's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $29,591M (+85.5%) with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B (+221%) and a fiscal Q4 guide of about $34.8B including $21.7B AI semiconductors (press coverage of the release). It sets the silicon (custom XPUs, Ethernet switches, retimers / DSPs) that decides copper versus optics per rack; it takes no connector share from APH directly. Its statements on scale-up Ethernet, copper and co-packaged optics were not retrieved (gap).

fd POTENTIAL (hypothesis, for the analyst): the bottleneck APH supplies is rack-level high-speed copper (backplane, board-to-board, cable assemblies) plus power and fiber interconnect for AI clusters; the shortage is demand-led (orders 1.23x sales) and is being met by APH's own capex; the copper window is attributed to run to about 2029 inside the rack (channel view), with Kyber midplane design the main named threat to cable-cartridge content and optics the long-run substitute beyond the rack.
